title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 3 findings on PR #524 head 4f3dcfb
description:
Supervisor self-review round 3 of PR #524 head 4f3dcfb. Round 2's seven findings are all confirmed fixed (6 of 97 observed failing against 97b2ff0 — see finding 9, the seventh test does not actually exercise its defect).

TEN findings. Finding 1 is a playability REGRESSION and is the priority. Findings 9-10 are a test-integrity class the supervisor found while doing the negative proof, and they explain how earlier rounds' defects survived.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev6 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev6, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 4f3dcfb. Run `npm ci` before verification.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (HIGH — regression, fix first) — an unresolvable rules binding now breaks EVERY turn.
=============================================================
contextAssembler.ts assembleContext now calls resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack(input.db, input.resolveRulesPack) unconditionally on the per-turn path. That function throws CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError for any binding it cannot resolve exactly. Before this branch, assembleContext never touched the binding, so an unresolvable binding degraded lookup_rules and the item/effect tools; now it throws inside the turn savepoint and the campaign is completely unplayable.
REPRODUCED at 4f3dcfb (supervisor), using the documented pre-adoption case — a DB bound to the retired placeholder RETIRED_DND5E_SRD_PLACEHOLDER_PACK_ID ('rules:dnd5e-srd'), which bundledSrdPack.ts says "fails resolution with a clear, actionable error":
    assembleContext -> CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError: campaign rules pack 'dnd5e-srd' / 'rules:dnd5e-srd' @ '5.1' is unavailable
The same applies to any campaign bound to a non-bundled base or add-on pack: packages/cli/src never supplies resolveRulesPack, so the CLI cannot satisfy it at all.
FIX: campaign-rule context must not be able to make a turn impossible. Degrade rather than throw — if the stack cannot be resolved, assemble the campaign-rule slice without pack-side ambiguity metadata and record that the ambiguity source was unavailable, so the DM still receives active campaign rules and the failure is visible rather than fatal. Do NOT silence the error; make it observable in the assembled context. Keep the strict behaviour for the paths that legitimately require an exact stack (lookup_rules, item/effect tools) — this fix is about the per-turn context path only.
EVIDENCE: a test with an unresolvable binding proving assembleContext succeeds, that active campaign rules are still supplied, and that the unavailability is represented in the result. Plus a test that a resolvable binding is unaffected.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 — m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds is permanently empty, so a probe closure assertion is vacuously true.
=============================================================
measurements.ts's new early return makes m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds always []. The first joinCampaignRules call is never conditional, so `asked` is always true, so rulingQueryExecuted is always true, so rulingQueryScope is always 'all-active', so the guard's first disjunct is unconditionally satisfied and the body below is unreachable. discoveryProbes.test.ts:220 asserts that array is empty as the closure invariant ("every ambiguity that reached the packet was offered to the seam") — that assertion can now never fail.
FIX: if all-active scope genuinely subsumes the check, say so explicitly and make the measurement state it, rather than leaving a dead computation behind a permanently-true guard and an assertion that proves nothing. Whatever you choose, the probe must once again be capable of failing when the property is violated.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 — the oracle seam ignores the new options argument, so probes assert a guarantee the double never provides.
=============================================================
test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts activeRulingsForAmbiguities ignores the second `options` parameter, while the production seam honours includeAllActive. Under the probes the trace therefore records rulingQueryScope 'all-active' and m5.allActiveRulingsRequested true while the fixture actually filtered by the requested ids. With finding 2 this means the probes record and assert a scope guarantee the double does not implement.
FIX: make the double honour includeAllActive exactly as the production seam does. This is the same class as eshyra-jhpt.2's original contract pinning: the oracle is the executable statement of the seam contract and must not drift from it.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 — the fixture-contract `continue` also skips the ruleIdentity check.
=============================================================
test/diagnostics/fixtureContract.ts:836-840 short-circuits before nonEmptyString(item.ruleIdentity, ...), not merely before the ambiguity-field checks. Every ruling case used to require a non-empty ruleIdentity; now a recurring-question ruling case may omit it, and oracleCampaignRules.ts substitutes item.caseId silently, so the omission is invisible.
FIX: hoist the ruleIdentity check above the continue.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 — revokedPosition and effectivePosition are still unvalidated against persisted chronology; only disputedPosition was fixed.
=============================================================
Round 2 finding 2 routed temporalMode.disputedPosition through assertPersistedPosition. revokeCampaignRule never validates input.revokedPosition that way, and create/supersede never validate effectivePosition that way. The only constraints are the ordering ones (>= effectivePosition, >= currentPosition). So a caller can revoke at a fabricated anchor — ordinal 999999 with invented session/turn ids — and because activeRows compares ordinal-first, the rule stays active for the realistic life of the campaign while the row claims a revocation at a turn that will never exist.
This is the same defect as round 2 finding 2, one field over. Fix the class, not the instance: every caller-supplied CampaignPosition that is persisted or compared against persisted chronology should go through the same validation. Enumerate them in your notes and say which ones you routed and why any were left out.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 — a dispute immediately after a session boundary is rejected.
=============================================================
campaignRules.ts immediatelyBefore requires disputedPosition.sessionId === currentPosition.sessionId. Ordinals are campaign-wide and unique (UNIQUE (campaign_id, ordinal)), so ordinal + 1 already identifies the preceding turn unambiguously. The consequence is that the first turn of a new session cannot dispute the last turn of the previous session — a realistic case, since a player may object to the last thing that happened when play resumes.
FIX: decide this deliberately and document the decision in the module. Default expectation: drop the sessionId requirement from immediatelyBefore, since the ordinal is already unique and authoritative, and keep sameTurn as-is. If you conclude cross-session disputes should stay forbidden, say why in the doc comment and add a test asserting the rejection is intentional rather than incidental.

=============================================================
FINDING 7 — failing closed on conflicting rulings can permanently wedge a campaign.
=============================================================
assembleCampaignRulesContext throws on multiple active rulings for one ambiguity, and it is now on the per-turn path. The single-active-ruling invariant is enforced only in application code; migration 0025 has no SQL constraint. A row arriving by any other route — checkpoint/Dolt restore, a direct write, a future importer — makes every turn throw and roll back, with no way to play or repair through the game.
The supervisor asked for fail-closed in round 1 and still wants the conflict surfaced rather than silently collapsed — but aborting every turn forever is too blunt.
FIX: surface the conflict in the projection so the DM context shows that the ambiguity has contradictory active rulings and that none is authoritative, instead of throwing. Keep a hard rejection at the ADMISSION boundary (assertNoOverlappingAmbiguityRuling), which is where it belongs. Test that a campaign holding a conflicting pair (inserted directly, as a restore would) is still playable and that the conflict is visible in the context.

=============================================================
FINDING 8 — a duplicate ambiguity id across records silently last-wins.
=============================================================
campaignContext.ts ambiguitiesFromStack does found.set(ambiguity.id, ambiguity), so when two different record keys in the resolved stack declare the same ambiguity id, the later silently replaces the earlier. optRulesAmbiguities only enforces id uniqueness WITHIN one record. Iteration is recordsByKey insertion order (base then add-ons), so an add-on overrides a base ambiguity by accident rather than by any stated precedence rule, changing the interpretations the DM is shown with no error and no trace.
FIX: either reject the collision loudly with both record keys in the message, or define and document an explicit precedence. Do not leave it to insertion order. Test the collision.

=============================================================
FINDING 9 (test integrity) — a committed regression test passes for the wrong reason and cannot fail.
=============================================================
test 'rejects a disputed anchor that disagrees with persisted chronology' (campaignRuleStore.test.ts:906) passes sessionId 'aaa-turn'/'zzz-turn' and turnId 'turn-1'/'turn-2' to resolveCampaignPosition — the session ids differ, so checkTemporalMode rejects on the SESSION mismatch and the anchor validation is never reached. The supervisor's negative proof observed 6 failures against 97b2ff0 where the report claimed 7; this is the missing one.
The FIX for that finding is genuinely present and correct — a correctly shaped test (same sessionId, differing turnIds, fabricated anchor) throws 'temporalMode.disputedPosition does not match the persisted campaign turn position' on this head and FAILS on 97b2ff0. Only the test is wrong.
Second confirmed instance: 'rejects direct creation of a revoked rule before its effective position' (campaignRuleStore.test.ts:978) omits currentPosition, so it trips 'currentPosition is required for live campaign rule creation' and has never exercised the guard in its name — it would still pass if that guard were deleted.
FIX: reshape both so they exercise the guard they name, and re-verify each fails against 4f3dcfb for the RIGHT reason.

=============================================================
FINDING 10 (test integrity, systemic — this is why the above was invisible) — negative tests assert only the error class.
=============================================================
All 28 negative assertions in campaignRuleStore.test.ts use bare toThrow(CampaignRuleError) with no message matching. The store now has roughly a dozen guards that fire in a fixed order, and earlier guards preempt later ones, so a test can pass on a guard other than the one it targets — which is exactly findings 9's two instances. Supervisor captured the messages; they are distinct and specific:
    backdated prospective create : prospective campaign rule cannot take effect before the current position
    stale currentPosition        : currentPosition does not match the persisted current campaign position
    duplicate identity           : campaign rule 'base' already exists
    revoke before effective      : campaign rule 'base' cannot be revoked before the current position
    supersede w/ backdated succ  : successor 's' cannot take effect before the current position
    cross-campaign supersede     : supersession cannot cross campaigns
FIX: every negative test in the campaign-rule suites must assert WHICH guard fired — toThrow(/distinctive message/) or an equivalent message assertion — not merely the error class. While doing so, check each test still trips its intended guard; report any further tests that were passing on the wrong one. This is the highest-value item here: it is what makes the rest of the suite mean what it says.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against 4f3dcfb; report the counts you actually observed, and for findings 9-10 confirm each reshaped test fails for the RIGHT reason (quote the message).
  - Do not weaken existing tests or assertions.
  - Do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, or the rejected relevance-selection finding (eshyra-umyb).
  - Keep every earlier fix intact.

VERIFICATION
`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local @eshyra/core resolution.

Completed in commit 9625708 on eshyra-jhpt.rev6; no push, PR, or changes outside this worktree. Fixed all ten findings. F1: assembleContext now degrades an unavailable rules binding, preserves active campaign rules, omits pack ambiguity metadata, and records/renders the exact CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError message. F2: M5 now explicitly reports ambiguityCoverage ('all-active' or 'requested-ambiguities'), and probes assert the declared all-active coverage. F3: oracleCampaignRuleSeam now honors includeAllActive exactly. F4: fixture ruleIdentity validation is before the ruling ambiguity continue. F5: caller-supplied revokedPosition is persisted-chronology validated; effectivePosition and successor.effectivePosition are validated when at/before current chronology while future prospective anchors remain schedulable; documented in the helper comment. F6: immediately preceding disputes may cross session boundaries because campaign ordinal is authoritative. F7: conflicting restored active rulings remain playable and render 'none is authoritative'. F8: duplicate ambiguity ids are rejected with both record keys. F9/F10: the disputed-anchor test now uses the same session with a fabricated turn id and asserts exactly 'temporalMode.disputedPosition does not match the persisted campaign turn position'; the revoked-before-effective test now exercises revokeCampaignRule and asserts exactly 'campaign rule \'bad-revoked\' cannot be revoked before its effective position'. All 28 campaignRuleStore negative assertions (and campaignRules negatives) now assert distinctive guard messages; no additional wrong-guard tests were found. Baseline regression proof against exact 4f3dcfb source: 10 focused tests failed as intended (F1 1, F2 1, F3 1, F4 1, F5 3, F6 1, F7 1, F8 1). F9/F10 are integrity reshapes over guards already present at 4f3dcfb, so they pass there while exact-message assertions prevent wrong-guard passes. Current focused suites: 118/118 passed. npm run verify:worktree passed from this worktree: 277 test files passed, 3 skipped; 4879 tests passed, 20 skipped; hidden-Unicode, format/lint/check, typecheck passed.
